name: Maba (Indonesia)
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Rødvand, Linn Iren Sjånes. 2024. Patani: Description of a South Halmahera–West New Guinea language. PhD thesis, University of Oslo. hdl:10852/115064.
sources.note: Grammar of the closest sister language Patani (pata1260), not of Maba. p. 9: Patani and Maba speakers say Maba is 'almost the same as Patani', author witnessed effortless mutual conversation. p. 10: only earlier sources for the area are Adriani & Kruijt 1914 'very brief sketch' and the Holle list. p. 435 fn. 27: 'I have not been able to track down any information on Patani's sister language Maba'. Patani stress sec. 2.5.1 pp. 64-66: not lexically contrastive; ultimate word stress the main pattern (49/62 polysyllables in isolation), 13 penultimate; possibly phrasal accent rather than word stre…

sources.citation: StressTyp2 (local SQL dump 2015-04-14) and WALS languages table (local copies).
sources.note: No entry for Maba (Indonesia) [mqa]; WALS 'mab' Maba is the Maban language of Chad (maba1277).

sources.citation: Ismail, Kalasun, Nurprihatina Hasan, Farida Maricar & Sulmi Magfirah. 2024. Multiple Meanings of Address Terms in Bicoli Language, South Maba, East Halmahera. IJOLEH 3(1). DOI 10.56314/ijoleh.v3i1.216.
sources.note: Sociolinguistic study of address terms in Bicoli (= Maba variety); no phonology; its references cite no Maba description. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Mujudin, Ona, Masayu Gay & Wa Ode Murima La Ode Alumu. 2022. Fungsi dan Pola Kalimat Bahasa Daerah Maba. KAMBOTI: Jurnal Sosial dan Humaniora 2(2): 108-115. DOI 10.51135/kambotivol2issue2page108-115.
sources.note: Sentence-pattern (S-P-O) description of Bahasa Daerah Maba only; states the language had not previously been studied; no phonology, nothing on stress (no 'tekanan', 'fonologi', 'suku kata' anywhere).

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera–West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, UC Berkeley.
sources.note: Maba data only second-hand (Adriani & Kruyt 1914; pronominal/verbal paradigms). Sec. 5.4 p. 117 lists SHWNG languages with described (penultimate) stress: Buli, Sawai, Taba, Ambai, Wandamen, Waropen, Warembori -- Maba not among them. No Maba stress statement.

sources.citation: Stokhof, W.A.L. & L. Saleh-Bronkhorst (eds). 1980. Holle lists: vocabularies in languages of Indonesia, Vol. 2: Sula and Bacan Islands, North Halmahera, South and East Halmahera. Pacific Linguistics D-28. Maba = list 168 (JB 1933), pp. 297-311.
sources.note: Maba list has only 'Basic data', wordlist, notes and 1931-questionnaire answers; no 'other details' paragraph on accent (such paragraphs exist for e.g. Sula Fagudu p. 67 and Galela p. 122, not for Maba). Nothing on Maba stress.

sources.citation: Blust, Robert. 1978. Eastern Malayo-Polynesian: a subgrouping argument. In Wurm & Carrington (eds), SICAL Proceedings, 181-234. Pacific Linguistics C-61.
sources.note: pp. 197-198: the only sketches are Adriani & Kruijt 1914 -- Buli 309-335 and 'thumbnail sketches of Maba (335-8), Patani (338-41), Sawai (341-4), Weda (344-5) and Gane (345-7)'; 'Maba is very closely related to Buli, perhaps being a dialect of the same language' (also Maan 1951: 5); Blust had a 200-item Swadesh list for Maba. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Maan, G. 1951. Proeve van een Bulische spraakkunst. VKI 10. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff.
sources.note: Buli grammar. p. 5: Maba (to be taken together with Bitjoli/Ingli, difference very small; c. 1800 speakers) borders Buli to the south. Maba appears only in comparative sound remarks (pp. 13-14). The Klemtoon section (sec. 3, p. 16) concerns Buli only. Nothing on Maba stress.

sources.citation: Hueting, A. 1908. Iets over de Ternataansch-Halmahèrasche taalgroep. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 60 (pp. 409-410 read via archive.org dli.ministry.10280).
sources.note: The klemtoon remarks on p. 409 concern Galela/Tobelo/Modole (North Halmahera); Maba, Bitjoli, Patani, Sawai, Weda, Gane are only listed (p. 410) as languages outside that group. Nothing on Maba stress.

sources.citation: Badan Pengembangan dan Pembinaan Bahasa. Peta Bahasa: 'Bahasa Patani', Provinsi Maluku Utara (idb=474).
sources.note: Treats Maba as 'dialek Maba' of Patani (data point Desa Soa Sangaji, Kec. Kota Maba, Halmahera Timur; 75.25% dialectometric difference from dialek Patani Tepeleo). No phonology; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Eberhard, David M., Gary F. Simons & Charles D. Fennig (eds). 2025. Ethnologue: Languages of the World, 28th ed. Entry 'Maba [mqa]'.

sources.citation: Adriani, N. & Alb. C. Kruijt. 1914. De Bare'e-sprekende Toradja's van Midden-Celebes, derde deel (Taal- en letterkundige schets der Bare'e-taal en overzicht van het taalgebied Celebes–Zuid-Halmahera). Batavia: Landsdrukkerij. Section 'Het taalgebied: Soela-eilanden – Zuid-Halmahera' pp. 288-347; Maba thumbnail sketch pp. 335-338 (Buli 309-335, Patani 338-341).
